info.title: AI Naples — track record API
info.description:
Read-only view over the Serie A prediction track record.

**The production model is M1**: the bookmaker's opening line with the margin
removed. Fair odds and overround are exposed because they are descriptive;
expected value, stakes and betting advice are not exposed at all — an EV
computed from M1's probabilities against the very odds they come from is
circular by construction, and measured to be negative on every single bet.

Writing happens only from local scheduled commands, never over HTTP.

get.summary: Every round with its state and archived RPS

schema.title: Response Get Rounds Api Rounds  Season  Get
Response Get Round Api Rounds  Season   Matchday  Get

get.summary: All matches of a season, filterable

schema.title: Response Get Matches Api Matches  Season  Get

get.description:
The table, computed from results — a fact, not a forecast.

Tied teams are separated head-to-head first, as Serie A does, and not by
goal difference: the shortcut produces a table that looks right and is
wrong exactly when the standings matter.

get.summary: The canonical M1 selections — no threshold to move
get.description:
The main line, and it takes no odds parameter on purpose.

These are the selections `predict_round` prints on Friday and the weekly
report shows, with `config.QUOTA_MINIMA_SELEZIONE` as the declared floor.
The band explorer (`/api/selections`) sits beside them as an adjustable
second reading: if a threshold chosen in the interface could redefine the
main line, the track record would be measuring one thing while the
dashboard advertised another.

get.summary: The same selections, from the machine-learning model (M5)
get.description:
The main line's rule — one pick per match, the likeliest among those whose
fair odds reach `config.QUOTA_MINIMA_SELEZIONE` — applied to M5's goal
expectations instead of M1's. Same code path as `/api/picks`, so the two
lists differ only in the model behind them.

A SECOND OPINION. M5 is indistinguishable from the market on the test
set: these picks are shown next to M1's, never instead of them, and the
track record stays M1's. Only matchdays M5 was run on appear.

get.summary: Markets priced under a ceiling on the odds

schema.description: Floor on the fair odds. Below it the market pays too little to be worth a bet; the band is the useful filter
schema.title: Min Odds

parameters.description: Floor on the fair odds. Below it the market pays too little to be worth a bet; the band is the useful filter

get.summary: The machine-learning model (M5) on a matchday, every market
get.description:
M5 as a second opinion, next to the market, on every derived market.

Same visibility as the matches: played ones are public, the ones still to
be played need `picks:read`. M5 is diagnostics — indistinguishable from
the market on the test set — and nothing here feeds the track record.
404 when M5 was not run on that matchday, or the deployment does not
mount `experiments/output/`.

get.summary: The machine-learning model (M5) on every match of one team
get.description:
M5 on a whole season of one team, for the "La mia squadra" screen.

One call instead of one per matchday: a season is 38 of them, and the
screen needs every match at once. Same payloads and same visibility as
`/api/ml/{season}/{matchday}` — this only gathers them. Matchdays M5 was
not run on are simply absent; an empty list is not an error.

get.summary: Last scheduler runs, current round, snapshot age

post.description:
Always 202, whether or not the address is already registered.

The account is created inactive; only the emailed link activates it. That
is what stops someone signing up with an address they do not own and then
using it.

schema.title: Response Signup Api Auth Signup Post

post.description: Confirms the address and signs the user in straight away.

A new access token from the refresh cookie, or 401.

Every check of a session happens HERE, on the row: revoked, past its 24
hours, idle too long, account no longer active. That is why an access token
can be trusted for its few minutes without the database — the moment it
lapses, the next one is only issued if the session still stands.

THE REFRESH TOKEN IS NOT ROTATED, and it is a choice. Rotation (a new
refresh token at every refresh, the old one dead) detects a stolen copy
only if the thief and the owner both use it — and it logs the owner out
whenever two tabs refresh at the same moment, since one of them presents a
token the other has just burnt. With a 24-hour ceiling and a sessions page
that revokes a device in one click, the race costs more than it buys.

Always 204, even without a valid session.

Signing out is not a place to report errors: if the cookie is already
unusable, the caller wanted exactly this state and gets it.

get.description: Who the cookie belongs to. The frontend calls this on load.

post.description: Always 202. A 404 here would make this an address checker.

schema.title: Response Forgot Password Api Auth Forgot Password Post

post.description:
Sets the new password and drops every session, including this one.

No cookie is issued: after a reset the user signs in again. If the reset
was triggered by someone else, that second step is where they stop.

schema.title: Response Reset Password Api Auth Reset Password Post

get.description:
Where this account is signed in.

IT IS THE ONLY WAY A USER CAN SEE A STOLEN COOKIE. The session is HttpOnly
and revocable server-side, which protects it from a script on the page but
says nothing to the person whose laptop was borrowed. A list with a time, a
place and a device is the thing they can actually read an intrusion out of.

schema.title: Response Sessions Api Auth Sessions Get

get.description:
What happened to this account lately: sign-ins, failures, password changes.

The sessions list shows who is signed in NOW. It cannot show eight wrong
passwords typed last night, and that is exactly the thing worth seeing
before it becomes a ninth that works.

schema.title: Response Activity Api Auth Activity Get

post.description:
Sign out everywhere else, keeping the session asking.

KEEPING THE CURRENT ONE IS THE POINT. Signing the user out of the page they
are using to secure their account is how a security action becomes one
nobody completes: they land on a login form and assume it failed.

schema.title: Response Revoke Other Sessions Api Auth Sessions Revoke Others Post

post.description:
Sign out one other device, the one the user does not recognise.

NOT THE CURRENT ONE: ending the session asking is sign-out, and it already
has its own route that also clears the cookie. Doing it here would leave a
dead cookie in the browser and a page that fails on its next request.

An id that belongs to another account answers exactly like one that does
not exist: 404, same body. Otherwise the route would confirm which session
ids are live, for anyone signed in.

schema.title: Response Revoke Session Api Auth Sessions  Session Id  Revoke Post

post.description: Every other session drops; the one doing the change survives.

Save the favourite team, or clear it with `null`.

The name must be a team of the current season, as the track record spells
it. A free string would be stored and never match a single fixture, and
the page would highlight nothing with no error anywhere.

get.description:
Matches not kicked off yet, with the model's price on every market.

Behind `picks:read`, like the unplayed rounds on the dashboard: the price
of a match that has not started is the product, here as there.

schema.title: Response Open Matches Api Me Predictions  Season  Open Get

get.description: Every pick of the season, newest match first, resolved against the result.

post.description:
Record one pick. 409 once the match has started, or if it is already there.

The kickoff is read from the match files, here, now. The request carries no
time at all, so there is nothing a client can send to make a late pick
look early.

schema.title: Response Add Prediction Api Me Predictions Post

post.description:
Withdraw a pick, before kick-off only.

After it, a deletion is how a losing pick would disappear from the
comparison: the same reason the track record is append-only. Another
account's pick answers 404, like one that does not exist.

schema.title: Response Delete Prediction Api Me Predictions  Pick Id  Delete Post

ActivityRow.title: ActivityRow
ActivityRow.description:
One entry of the account's own audit trail, as its owner sees it.

NO `details`. That column holds context for whoever investigates — the id
of the admin who granted a role, the reason of a refusal — and none of it
is the user's to read. What is left is what a person can act on: what
happened, whether it worked, when, from where.

MLRound.title: MLRound
MLRound.description:
M5 on a matchday. DIAGNOSTICS, not the production model.

On the test set M5 is indistinguishable from the market, so the track
record stays on M1. Nothing here feeds a metric.

kickoff_utc.title: Kickoff Utc
kickoff_utc.description: ISO 8601 UTC. Null when the match is not in the calendar

match_date.title: Match Date
match_date.description: ISO 8601 UTC midnight of the scheduled day, as logged

overround.title: Overround
overround.description: Book margin: sum of implied probabilities minus one

result_source.title: Result Source
result_source.description: football-data, understat or fbref. Null when unplayed, or archived before the source was recorded

rps.title: Rps
rps.description: Ranked Probability Score, lower is better. Null if the match is unplayed or the row is invalid

Match.title: Match
Match.description:
One prediction, with its result when there is one.

`status` is the field to branch on:
  predicted  in the log, not played yet          -> every result field null
  played     played, round not closed yet        -> result yes, metrics null
  resolved   played, archived, metrics computed  -> everything valued
  invalid    played, but written after kickoff   -> result yes, metrics null

`played` is PROVISIONAL: the score comes from the same source chain
`close_round` uses, the evening of the match, but it is not on record
until the round is closed. football-data may still publish an official
score that differs (a match awarded 0-3), and metrics are computed only
from the archive.

`invalid` is not a bug to hide: the log is append-only and keeps its own
mistakes. `valid` and `invalid_reason` exist so the frontend can say why a
played match has no RPS instead of showing an unexplained hole.

OddsSnapshot.title: OddsSnapshot
OddsSnapshot.description:
The upcoming-odds file. An EMPTY snapshot is a normal state between rounds,
not a failure: football-data answers but has not published the round yet.

OpenMatch.title: OpenMatch
OpenMatch.description: A match that can still be picked, with the model's price on every market.

min_odds.title: Min Odds
min_odds.description: The declared floor, config.QUOTA_MINIMA_SELEZIONE. Not a request parameter: the main line cannot be re-cut per call

Picks.title: Picks
Picks.description:
The canonical selections. No threshold field to move, by design.

`most_probable` is the most likely market of each match, whatever it pays;
`with_min_odds` is the most likely among those paying at least `min_odds`,
which comes from `config.QUOTA_MINIMA_SELEZIONE` and not from the request.
Both are the rules the project has used since the first registered round.

Refreshed.title: Refreshed
Refreshed.description: When the new access token lapses, and when the session behind it does.

Round.title: Round
Round.description:
A matchday and where it stands.

`status` is translated from the project's single state machine
(`rounds.stato_giornate`), never recomputed here: future, open, predicted,
partially_predicted, played, closed.

SeasonSummary.title: SeasonSummary
SeasonSummary.description:
Headline figures. Hits keep numerator and denominator apart on purpose: a
bare rate hides how thin the sample is, and right now it is very thin.

`rps_backtest_reference` is 0.1881, the market's RPS on the test set. A
persistent gap from it would not be a model getting things wrong — the
model *is* the opening line — it would be the production pipeline behaving
differently from the backtest.

market.title: Market
market.description: Raw market name, e.g. 1X, over 2.5, casa segna

book_odds.title: Book Odds
book_odds.description: Registered bookmaker price. Only 1X2 has one

won.title: Won
won.description: Null while the match is unplayed

Selection.title: Selection
Selection.description:
One market of one match, priced by the model.

`fair_odds` is 1/p — the price at which the bet would break even. It exists
for every market. `book_odds` exists only for 1X2, because that is all the
register stores: for double chance, over/under and goal markets the price
has to come from the reader's own bookmaker, and estimating it by applying
an average margin would be a made-up number that looks measured.

excluded_markets.title: Excluded Markets
excluded_markets.description: Near-certainties never returned: no book prices them high enough to be a bet, and at a low ceiling they would crowd out everything else

matches_total.title: Matches Total
matches_total.description: Matches with a prediction in the requested scope

matches_covered.title: Matches Covered
matches_covered.description: Of those, how many have at least one market inside the band. A narrow band leaves matches uncovered, and the gap is reported rather than hidden

best_per_match.title: Best Per Match
best_per_match.description: One selection per match: the most probable inside the band, highest odds breaking a tie. Recomputed from the stored lambdas, never frozen into the register

Selections.title: Selections
Selections.description:
Selections inside an odds band, with hits and their denominator.

The numbers travel together on purpose: "10 su 11" says what "91%" hides,
which is that eleven bets decide nothing. Filtering by odds moves variance,
not edge — M1's probabilities are the book's own line with the margin
removed, so expected value is minus the margin at every threshold.

SessionRow.title: SessionRow
SessionRow.description:
One active session, as its owner sees it.

NO TOKEN AND NO HASH. The point of storing only the digest is that reading
the table does not let anyone impersonate anyone; putting either on the
wire would give that back. `current` is what the page needs instead —
enough to say "this is the one you are using now" without naming it.

tolerance.title: Tolerance
tolerance.description: RPS gap from the backtest worth detecting (config.TRACK_TOLERANCE_RPS)

Significance.title: Significance
Significance.description:
How far the track record is from meaning something.

The bootstrap resamples ROUNDS, not matches: the ten matches of a round are
predicted by the same fit, and treating them as independent would shrink
the interval by about sqrt(10) and make anything look significant.
Under four rounds there is nothing to resample, and the method says so.

form.title: Form
form.description: Ultimi risultati in ordine di data, dal piu' vecchio: W, D, L. Dai totali non si ricava — la sequenza e' proprio l'informazione che interessa

Standings.title: Standings
Standings.description:
La classifica: aritmetica sui risultati, non una previsione.

`tie_break` dichiara come sono separate le squadre a pari punti, perche' in
Serie A contano prima gli scontri diretti e non la differenza reti — una
tabella ordinata nel modo sbagliato sembra giusta proprio nelle settimane
in cui qualcuno la guarda.

Status.title: Status
Status.description:
Enough for a frontend to show that the system is alive — and no way to
command it. Writing happens only from local processes.

Summary.title: Summary
Summary.description:
The comparison without a score.

`mean_model_probability` is what the model expected of the resolved picks
on average; `hit_rate` is what actually happened. Side by side they say
whether the user's picks did better or worse than the model thought they
would — the one honest comparison with no points table.

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.description: Null below 50 resolved predictions: fewer points make a curve that is noise drawn nicely
